concerns: Authentication is based on the unverified 'X-Moodle-Role' and 'X-User-Id' HTTP headers, which poses a spoofing risk if not stripped or injected securely by an upstream gateway/reverse proxy. Real security should rely on a Spring Security filter chain with token (JWT) verification.
Role checks use hardcoded string literals ('admin', 'content_manager', 'admin_user') within the controller instead of leveraging standard Spring Security authorities, enums, or a permission matrix.
If 'X-User-Id' is null or invalid, the audit log will still be saved with a null user. It is recommended to have a fallback audit user or reject unauthenticated delete operations entirely.
The delete API endpoint method in the controller is annotated directly with '@Transactional'. It is better practice to keep transactional boundaries encapsulated within a service layer.
